sections.h2: Where is Haralson County and who runs its property tax?
sections.html:
Haralson County sits in northwest Georgia on the Alabama line. It covers 282 square miles and was carved out of Carroll and Polk counties in 1856 as Georgia's 113th county. Buchanan is the county seat, and the county's own website puts the population near 30,000. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 33,066, up 10.5% from the April 2020 base.

Two offices share the property tax work. The Board of Tax Assessors appraises every parcel and takes homestead applications, and the Tax Commissioner prepares the digest, bills the tax and collects it. The commissioner has no say over value or millage; those come from the assessors and from the county commissioners and the other taxing bodies such as cities and schools.

  • Board of Tax Assessors: 4266 GA Highway 120, Buchanan, 770-646-2022, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-646-2020 for payment and billing questions.
  • Towns inside the county: Bremen, Buchanan, Tallapoosa and Waco. Ask the clerk in the town where the house sits whether it sends its own bill.

sections.h2: What towns and neighborhoods affect a Haralson County sale?
sections.html:
Haralson County has four incorporated places and three small unincorporated communities. Bremen is the largest city, at about 6,500 residents, followed by Tallapoosa at roughly 3,155, Buchanan at 1,159 and Waco at 522. Budapest, Draketown and Felton are unincorporated.

Each town has its own story, and that shapes the houses you find there. Bremen grew around the railroad and became known as a clothing capital of the Southeast, with men's suits shipped nationwide. Tallapoosa, the Dogwood City, began as a gold mining town and opened Georgia's first free school in 1889. Buchanan's 1891 courthouse still stands on the square, and Waco is home to West Georgia Technical College. The county also lists a major hospital and two public school systems, so the school district a house falls in is worth checking during a sale.

Georgia's revenue department notes that cities can levy their own ad valorem tax and that the city clerk bills it, unless the city and county agreed to a single bill. A Bremen or Tallapoosa address can therefore mean two statements, while a house in an unincorporated community like Felton or Draketown sees only the county bill.

sections.h2: When are Haralson County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Property taxes are due December 1 each year, and mobile home taxes are due April 1. After the due date, interest is added monthly at a rate tied to the prime rate, and a penalty of 5% attaches each 120 days, up to a total of 20%.

Georgia's revenue department adds that a taxpayer gets 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest accrues. The county's tax calculation page spells out how the bill is built: the assessors' value times 40 percent gives the assessed value, and the millage rate from the commissioners and other levying bodies is applied to that figure. One mill equals $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

The Tax Commissioner's office also handles tag renewals, titles, mobile home decals, timber tax and handicap placards. The title desk stops processing at 4 p.m., so plan a closing-day errand with that in mind. The county posts a notice each year with the current digest and the five year history of the levy, as Georgia law requires.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Haralson County valuation?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Board of Assessors by the deadline printed on your annual notice. For 2025, the notices were mailed June 6 and the appeal deadline was Monday, July 21, which has passed.

The assessors explain that fair market value means what a knowledgeable buyer would pay a willing seller in an arm's length sale. The notice also shows estimated taxes based on the prior year's millage, so the real bill can differ once the commissioners and the Board of Education set rates, usually between July and August.

Haralson County's appeals volume has been heavy. The assessors' page states that appeals passed the 3 percent threshold in O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, which gives the board an extra 180 days to decide and notify owners. Anyone with an open appeal can call 770-646-2022 or email the assessors for status. Field appraisers may visit a property under O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 and carry photo identification in a marked county vehicle.

sections.h2: Which Haralson County exemptions and programs matter to sellers and owners?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the common one, and the Haralson County page tells owners to file with the Tax Commissioner's office. You must have owned the home on January 1 and applied by April 1, when returns are due. A late application waits until the next calendar year.

  • Homestead: covers the home and the land beneath it when it is your legal residence. A person away for health reasons is not denied, and a family member or friend can notify the office for them.
  • Conservation use and preferential agricultural assessment: both use a 10 year covenant, and apply between January 2 and April 1. The county says preferential assessment generally gives a 25 percent advantage, and conservation use can save more than 50 percent in some cases.
  • Residential transitional assessment: a 10 year covenant for land moving from residential to commercial use.

Covenants matter in a sale. A farm or timber tract under a 10 year covenant carries obligations the buyer has to continue, so ask the Specialized Assessment department at the assessors' office what a transfer does to the covenant before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What should a Haralson County seller do about the tax bill?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Commissioner at 770-646-2020 what is owed on the parcel and whether the current year's bill has been issued. Bills fall due December 1, so a closing earlier in the year often happens before the statement exists, and the contract has to say who covers that gap.

Interest and penalties stack up after the due date. Interest is added monthly, a penalty of 5% attaches at each 120 day mark, and the total penalty stops at 20%. A buyer's title search will pick up unpaid taxes, so a written payoff figure from the commissioner helps the closing attorney.

  • Confirm whether you filed for homestead by April 1 and whether it applies to the buyer's first year.
  • For a mobile home, remember the April 1 due date, which is separate from the December 1 bill on land.
  • If the land is under a conservation or preferential agricultural covenant, ask the assessors what a transfer does to it.

sections.h2: How does Haralson County's housing market compare?
sections.html:
Haralson County is mid-priced for rural west Georgia. The Census Bureau QuickFacts table shows a median owner-occupied home value of $227,500 for 2020 to 2024, a median household income of $72,127 and a median gross rent of $923.

Workers here spend a mean 33.8 minutes getting to work, the second longest commute of the four counties compared in the Census table. Land area is 282.17 square miles with about 106 people per square mile, so the county is far less crowded than Hall County to the northeast and far busier than Hancock County to the east.

faqs.q: When is Haralson County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 1 each year, with mobile home tax due April 1. After the due date, interest is added monthly at a rate tied to prime, and a 5% penalty is added for every 120 days, with a 20% cap.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Haralson County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner's office at 770-646-2020 for billing and payment. Value and appeal questions go to the Board of Tax Assessors at 770-646-2022.

faqs.q: What is the Haralson County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1. You must have owned the home on January 1 and filed by the date returns are due, and a later application is not granted until the next calendar year.

faqs.q: Does Haralson County offer a break for farmland?
faqs.a: Yes. Conservation use and preferential agricultural assessment both require a 10 year covenant, and applications run January 2 through April 1. The county says preferential assessment generally gives a 25 percent advantage over fair market value.

faqs.q: Why is my Haralson County appeal taking so long?
faqs.a: Appeals passed 3 percent of parcels or digest value, so O.C.G.A. 48-5-311 gives the assessors an extra 180 days to rule. Call 770-646-2022 or email the assessors for the status of your appeal.
